title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

Tom B. Brown*    Benjamin Mann*    Nick Ryder*    Melanie Subbiah*

Amanda Askell    Sandhini Agarwal    Ariel Herbert-Voss    Gretchen Krueger    Tom Henighan

Benjamin Chess    Jack Clark    Christopher Berner

OpenAI

Abstract

Recent work has demonstrated substantial gains on many NLP tasks and benchmarks by pre-training on a large corpus of text followed by fine-tuning on a specific task. While typically task-specific in architecture, this method still requires task-specific fine-tuning datasets of thousands or tens of thousands of examples. By contrast, humans can generally perform a new language task from only a few examples or from simple instructions – something which current NLP systems still largely struggle with. Here we show that scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance, sometimes even reaching competitiveness with prior state-of-the-art fine-tuning approaches.
